cases.source: ICO, DPP Law Ltd, monetary penalty £60,000, 14 Apr 2025 (UK GDPR Arts 5(1)(f), 32(1), 32(2), 33(1)). https://ico.org.uk/action-weve-taken/enforcement/2025/04/dpp-law-ltd
cases.regulator_found: A law firm lost 32 GB of client data to ransomware; weak security and late breach notification (press reports: an old high-privilege account without MFA, 43 days to notify).
cases.beyond_questionnaire: The 43-day delay is an operational failure; a questionnaire can only check that a breach owner and a 72-hour procedure exist (document 07).

cases.source: Datatilsynet (Denmark), SIRIUS law firm, fine EUR 67,200, 14 Jul 2022 (GDPR Art. 32). https://www.enforcementtracker.com/ETid-1270
cases.regulator_found: Hackers encrypted the firm's servers; basic measures missing, including multi-factor login.
cases.beyond_questionnaire: Whether patches were applied is not asked.

cases.source: UODO (Poland), court bailiff, fines EUR 4,935, decision 23 Oct 2025 (GDPR Arts 33(1), 34(1)-(2)). https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/polish-sa-administrative-fine-of-4-935-eur-for-bailiff-for-failure-to-notify-a-personal-data_lt
cases.regulator_found: A letter with name, PESEL, address and amount went to the wrong person; the office judged the risk 'unlikely' without any risk analysis and notified no one.
cases.beyond_questionnaire: The missing risk analysis after the incident; the pack's breach procedure (07) asks for one, but only a drill shows it is used.

cases.source: Garante (Italy), OpenAI, EUR 15 million, decision 2 Nov 2024, published 20 Dec 2024. Reported annulled on appeal in March 2026: check before citing. https://www.garanteprivacy.it/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/10085432
cases.regulator_found: No legal basis identified before processing started; the legitimate-interest assessment was written only when the Garante asked; transparency gaps; no age check; a breach was not notified.
cases.beyond_questionnaire: Age verification is not asked (a law firm's agents rarely face the public).

cases.source: KVKK Board, decision 2020/26 (14 Jan 2020): a lawyer disclosed personal data to third parties by SMS; administrative fine reported as 50,000 TL. https://kvkk.gov.tr/Icerik/6697/2020-26
cases.regulator_found: A lawyer, as controller, sent a debtor's data to other people by text message.
cases.beyond_questionnaire: Who the lawyer chooses to message is a professional decision, not a system design; Uyum can only flag outputs that leave the firm unchecked.

cases.source: KVKK Board, decision 2022/249 (17 Mar 2022): a technology company kept data on cloud servers abroad without a m.9 basis. https://www.kvkk.gov.tr/Icerik/7558/2022-249
cases.regulator_found: Hosting on a foreign cloud is a transfer abroad; it needed a KVKK m.9 mechanism.

cases.source: KVKK Board, WhatsApp decision (2021): 1,950,000 TL for a bundled consent and transfers abroad without a valid basis. https://www.kvkk.gov.tr/Icerik/7045/WHATSAPP-UYGULAMASI-HAKKINDA-YURUTULEN-RESEN-INCELEMEYE-ILISKIN-KAMUOYU-DUYURUSU
cases.regulator_found: Transfers abroad without explicit consent or a Board-approved undertaking.
cases.beyond_questionnaire: A personal WhatsApp account is a common real channel; the questionnaire only sees it if the firm lists it as a vendor.

cases.source: Garante (Italy), urgent limitation order against the DeepSeek chatbot, 30 Jan 2025 (data stored in China, insufficient answers on transfers). https://www.garanteprivacy.it
cases.regulator_found: Personal data sent to servers in China with no transfer mechanism.

cases.source: KVKK Board guide for lawyers (22 Sep 2026), p. 146: mask or anonymise before using AI tools; uploading client files to generative AI can be a transfer abroad. https://www.kvkk.gov.tr/Icerik/8990/
cases.regulator_found: Guidance, not a decision: a lawyer pastes client files into a free consumer chatbot.

cases.source: KVKK Board, decision 2023/1414: a lawyer submitted special-category (health) data to a court file. https://kvkk.gov.tr/Icerik/7780/2023-1414
cases.regulator_found: Whether processing health data for a court submission had a m.6/3 condition and was necessary.
cases.beyond_questionnaire: Necessity for the specific claim is a legal judgment per file.

cases.source: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (NL), Clearview AI, EUR 30.5 million, Sep 2024: scraped public data into profiles of people.
cases.regulator_found: Building profiles of people from public sources without a legal basis or information to them.

cases.source: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(d), prohibited since 2 Feb 2025: predicting a person's risk of committing a crime from profiling alone.
cases.regulator_found: Rule, not a decision: a DD agent scores individuals' criminal risk.
